svg.text: One deployment, two seats, one remote state
One placement for four documents, shared by tkr and tkp; a second seat joins through the signed publication; one lease and per-document CAS guard every write.

text.tspan: "state": { "backend": "local" }
"state": { "backend": "s3",
"bucket": "…", "region": "…", "prefix": "…" }
one DeploymentStateLocation for all four documents; no verb may pick
its own backend. Local is the default. S3 is a create-time choice:
--state-bucket, --state-region, --state-prefix, all or none. The bucket's
region is recorded on its own and may differ from the provider region.

svg.text: workflow history and DSQL do not move

text.tspan: envelope state/envelope <prefix>/envelope
infrastructure state/infra <prefix>/infra
runtime state/deploy <prefix>/deploy
operation lease state/lock/operation <prefix>/lock/operation
tkr and tkp each derive the bundle from the same metadata — it is never
passed through argv or the environment — and thread its four handles
through the whole verb. The envelope coordinates the lifecycle; infra and
runtime state stay separate documents. The platform declaration never
chooses state placement.
<prefix>/envelope/manifest.json the head — ETag CAS
<prefix>/envelope/snapshots/<ts>-<uuid>.json immutable, create-only
a save is one protocol: check the head's ETag, take a short save lease on it,
upload the snapshot create-only, commit the new head with If-Match. A lost
race is a Conflict; an unreferenced snapshot is harmless. Loads follow the
head and verify the snapshot's SHA-256
the operation lease is one CAS-guarded record: acquire · renew · adopt ·
release, a 120 s TTL renewed every 40 s while a command runs

svg.text: SEAT A — CREATE WITH REMOTE STATE

text.tspan: tkr deployment create --name shared --platform compose \
--state-bucket <bucket> --state-region <region> --state-prefix <prefix> \
--build-image <image>@sha256:<digest>

svg.text: the bucket is primordial and operator-owned
s3:GetObject + s3:PutObject over the prefix, ambient identity
Creation under the lease — while still staged

text.tspan: acquire <prefix>/lock/operation as tkr-create — the lease closes the
race between checking a prefix and committing to it
read the envelope, infra, and deploy heads: any non-empty head refuses
— "prefix already contains deployment state; choose an unused prefix
or fetch its signed publication"
commit the creation envelope { deployment id, binding, integrity,
revision 0 } with a create-only save; release the lease
only then the local atomic rename makes the deployment visible

svg.text: local commit fails after the remote commit → snapshots stay, the prefix stays reserved

text.tspan: the signed Deployment Claim records
state = { bucket, region, prefix } beside
the definition half and the engine half —
never a credential
the repository itself is provisioned
locally at create (repositories/<name>);
its S3 home is reached through the
repository remotes — one verification
path over both homes

svg.text: publication failure is pending, never an unwind
The command — another machine, the same deployment

text.tspan: tkr deployment fetch --name shared \
--repository s3://<bucket>/<base>/<name> --trust-anchor root.json
the pinned root.json is the only thing trusted out of
band; the TUF chain proves which metadata is current
and what every target must hash to, with freshness
enforced
the claim must agree with every target across both
halves, or nothing materializes
the plan places the definition root and companions,
the config tree, tkp for this host, and the sidecar —
into an invisible staging directory
metadata.json is synthesized from the claim: the
state location comes from the claim, not from flags

svg.text: Join the remote envelope — no creation write

text.tspan: verify the placed tkp against its sidecar, then load
<prefix>/envelope and refuse unless all four agree
with the publication:
deployment id
engine binding (version · sha · tree hash · mode)
integrity manifest
configuration revision
retain the revision's source set, then the atomic
rename — the seat now forwards to its own tkp over
the state seat A created

svg.text: a revision mismatch refuses: publish the committed transition first

text.tspan: exactly one thing, out of band: the pinned root.json. Which metadata is current,
which targets exist, and what bytes they must hash to arrive through the signed
chain — root, targets, snapshot, timestamp — enforced on load and on every read.
Expiry fails closed; the datastore under state/repository/ remembers trusted
versions, so a rewound repository is refused as rollback
the earlier design hand-rolled digests, an evidence envelope, and an authority
policy that The Update Framework already standardizes — and lacked what TUF adds:
freshness against a frozen repository and rollback detection. The spike proved the
fit before the spec committed: consistent snapshots yield exactly the create-only S3
layout (only timestamp.json ever mutates); the transport is one GetObject; tamper,
rollback, and freeze are refused; keys rotate in place; KMS can hold role keys

svg.text: theupdateframework.io · The Update Framework 1.0 via tough 0.24 · proven in the spike, PR #81

text.tspan: the Deployment Claim, signed custom metadata on the definition root's target,
binds the definition half to the engine half and carries the state location
publications are monotonic and derived from committed state — the envelope
stays the commit authority, a failed publication is pending, never an unwind
one write policy in two homes: create-only objects first, mutable heads last

svg.text: EVERY VERB — TWO PROCESSES, ONE LEASE, ANY SEAT

text.tspan: route by metadata's definition record, never file presence
open the envelope from the recorded location to classify the verb:
read-only · bound mutation · dev candidate · upgrade · rollback
a bound mutation re-hashes <dir>/tkp against the envelope's
integrity manifest for this host target before anything runs
<dir>/tkp <verb…> --deployment-dir <dir> [--yes]
spawned with inherited stdio; the exit status propagates verbatim.
Read-only verbs run with no lock and no gate, so a blocked deployment
stays diagnosable from any seat.
reads metadata.json itself, validates the placed bundle, and prepares the
same four handles — the S3 client for the recorded bucket region
admission and the gate spine, then with_operation_lock around the
mutation: acquire <prefix>/lock/operation, renew every 40 s, refuse if held
("another provisioner may be operating this deployment")
probe, then mutate; infra and runtime state save after every transition;
the envelope's CAS commit advances the config revision; the transition
publishes to the repository; the lease releases

svg.text: rollback: tkr acquires, hands holder + token by env, both tkp launches adopt — one lock

text.tspan: the lease serializes mutations across seats: a second mutating
command does not wait — it refuses while another provisioner
holds the lease
a seat that saves from a stale document loses its CAS and
gets Conflict — never an overwrite, never a torn head
retained source revisions are per seat; the envelope and its
revision are shared, so every seat's describe reads the same
truth. Local state is not portable: fetching a local-state
publication yields a fresh local envelope, not a shared seat

svg.text: tkr deployment lock is a local mis-apply guard, not this lease
tkp destroy under the lease tears down provider resources

text.tspan: "remote state retained at s3://<bucket>/<prefix>" — manifests, snapshots, and the released lock record stay as
recovery and audit material; bucket policy and lifecycle decide removal, and a later create never reuses the prefix
